method: Manually scored in-session by reading each module's README.md and title image directly (Claude as the multimodal judge), 2026-09-21.
caveat: These are PRESENTATION-quality scores (photos/description/consistency) only. They do not and cannot capture sourcing/EOL/reliability issues a human maintainer knows about. Example: ISM03 scores high on presentation (~80) but the maintainer set mark=30, because open issues on the ISM03 repo (#1 'Migration to Si4468', #2 'Patching the Si4x6x-C2A Devices') show the core chip (Si4463) is going EOL / needs a firmware patch. Sellability = presentation quality AND procurement/reliability status; this tool only automates the former. Never silently overwrite a human-set mark -- report the diff instead.

anchors.why: Only image in metadata is a QR code (no product photo at all) -> automatic photos=0. Description is a 2-sentence stub using an old template. No contradiction found, but nothing to verify against either.
Sharp, clean, well-lit real product photo with clear on-board labeling. README is 2 sentences, no features/pinout table despite the photo showing a full pinout. Text and image don't contradict.

Clean legible KiCad render (bare board, connectors labeled, matches MCX-input description). README has headings, features, typical applications, a parts table -- but has a leftover AI-draft citation artifact '〉X†file.pdf】'-style token, docked for that.

Professional studio product photo (angled, clean background, all pins legible). README has a parameters table and a sales pitch (this module is one UST sells) -- minor typos only. Validates the rubric against a human anchor: automated 91 vs human 90.

By presentation alone this is one of the best READMEs seen (structured, links, real-world usage example from a third party). Human mark of 30 reflects EOL risk on the core chip, invisible from docs/photos -- see caveat above. Report both, do not overwrite.
Render shows a bare, unpopulated PCB with no cell holders visible -- technically clean/sharp but doesn't convey what a '4x LTO cell holder' actually looks like or does. README is one sentence.
Sharp studio photo, all labeling legible. Matches human anchor closely (88 vs 90).

Real photo, sharp, but on a wood-desk background rather than neutral -- older/busier board. README is short (519B) relative to the module's complexity (FPGA school board) despite having 24 images available. Close to human anchor (55 vs 60).
